news.title: Trump Administration Ratchets Up Export Control Penalties
news.summary_en: Penalties for export control violations are rising, while government-led training and outreach has slowed, making effective compliance programs more critical than ever. Pending legislation could raise fines even higher.

news.title: U.S.-India Insight: India’s Trade Deals: Only a Starting Point to Progress
news.summary_en: India's trade deals with Australia and the UAE have boosted bilateral trade significantly, but neither partner has meaningfully shifted in India's overall trade mix. The real work lies in domestic reform, not deal-making.

news.title: Innovation Lightbulb: Non-Resident Patents Are a Sign of U.S. Innovation Strength
news.summary_en: High levels of foreign patenting reflect an important U.S. strength: an innovation ecosystem that attracts globally valuable technologies, expertise, and investment.

news.title: Fueling Discontent
news.summary_en: This installment of Charting the Middle East traces the rapid rise in government-set fuel prices in Syria, highlighting how the Iran war’s economic effects are introducing new risks to regional stability.

news.title: Kim’s Second Byungjin: 21 Years After the Six-Party Talks Agreement
news.summary_en: North Korea is pursuing a “second byungjin” that advances its nuclear program while also seeking to normalize relations with countries willing to tolerate (if not necessarily accept) North Korea as a nuclear power.

news.title: Is Venezuela Moving Toward Democracy?
news.summary_en: More than nine months after the capture of Nicolás Maduro, CSIS Americas Program Acting Director and Senior Fellow Christpher Hernandez-Roy and Antonella Navarro assess Venezuela's progress towards political transition.

news.title: Project Vault Moves from Concept to Execution
news.summary_en: Project Vault is moving from concept to execution. Glencore and Mercuria are committing $1 billion to source and stockpile critical minerals for U.S. manufacturers, putting the United States’ first commercial strategic minerals reserve into motion.

news.title: The Melting Arctic Lifeline for Russia’s Shadow Fleet
news.summary_en: Two floating storage vessels have handled an estimated 53 percent of Russia’s seaborne Arctic crude exports since February 2022. CSIS Futures Lab analysis shows how the United States and Europe can target these bottlenecks to constrain the Kremlin’s wartime revenue.
